title: Cheap RAG in Go with Gemini File Search: no vector DB, two calls, one hosted store
why_read: A practical, concrete walkthrough of building a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation system in Go using Gemini's hosted File Search instead of a self-managed vector database.
analysis: This post describes building a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) tool in Go using Google's Gemini File Search API, which handles chunking, embedding, and indexing documents automatically on Google's servers. The author explicitly avoids building a traditional RAG stack of vector database, embedding pipeline, chunker, and reranker, instead relying on just two API calls to a hosted document store. This is useful and practical for engineers who want a fast, low-maintenance way to build grounded, citation-backed retrieval tools without managing infrastructure themselves. The post promises to cover specific pitfalls encountered along the way, which could be valuable for anyone considering the same approach.
